strings.name: Frida Kahlo
strings.role: Painter · Exploring the body and identity through self-portraiture
strings.summary: Frida Kahlo was a Mexican painter known for her self-portraits and richly symbolic works. Chronic pain after a traffic accident, her relationship with Diego Rivera, Mexican culture and her political views all entered her art. She transformed personal experience into a distinctive visual language. Her work was exhibited in New York and Paris during her lifetime and later became a key reference in discussions of the body, women’s experiences and cultural identity.
strings.coverageNote: Selected, verifiable life events and works. Dates follow the cited institutions; this is not a day-by-day chronology.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: National Preparatory School; largely self-taught as a painter
strings.facts.fact-03.label: Notable works
strings.facts.fact-03.value: The Two Fridas, The Broken Column, Henry Ford Hospital
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: A visual language of personal experience
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Works such as The Two Fridas and The Broken Column explore the body, emotion and self-image.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: International exhibitions and reach
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Held her first solo exhibition in New York in 1938 and took part in an exhibition in Paris in 1939, expanding her international influence.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Dies in Mexico
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Died aged 47. Records of her life and work at the Blue House later became important resources for studying her.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Solo exhibition in Mexico
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Lola Álvarez Bravo organized a solo exhibition; ill and confined to bed, Kahlo attended the opening in a bed.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Paints The Broken Column
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Used images of a fractured body and supporting structures to express the experience of chronic illness and pain.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Paints The Two Fridas
strings.timeline.event-04.text: This double self-portrait became one of her major explorations of emotion and identity.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: First solo exhibition in New York
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Exhibited at the Julien Levy Gallery and travelled to Paris for an exhibition the following year.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Paints Henry Ford Hospital
strings.timeline.event-06.text: While living in the United States, addressed bodily and reproductive experiences through painting, developing a distinctive symbolic expression.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Marries Rivera
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Married the Mexican muralist Diego Rivera; their relationship also became a subject in her paintings.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Paints an early self-portrait
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Began painting during her lengthy recovery from the accident and completed her first self-portrait as a gift for her lover.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Suffers a serious traffic accident
strings.timeline.event-09.text: The bus she was riding collided with a tram. She was severely injured and underwent repeated treatment for the rest of her life.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Coyoacán
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in the family home in Mexico City that later became known as the Blue House.
